Start here: make the BSPD trip

Three steps, about a minute. Everything you see is computed live from the board's real circuit.

  1. 1
    Run the BSPD test

    Loads the Scrut Test, mandatory in electrical scrutineering (10 turns × 0.833 A through the current sensor = 5 kW at 600 V) and presses the brake fully for 2 s.

  2. 2
    Follow the chain

    In the block diagram, brake and current go high, Q1 starts the 0.5 s timer (C7 charges), then IC1 drops the relay. The strip above gives the trip delay against the 500 ms rule.

  3. 3
    Change a threshold, test again

    Open Advanced calibration, turn T0.5 or CTH and run the test again. Click any block to see the real parts in the schematic.

Note: the board schematic labels the shutdown circuit SC (SC_IN, SC_OUT), but the correct Formula Student name is SDC.

What the LEDs mean
  • PWR — the 5 V rail is up.
  • P_TH — brake pressure is above PTH (hard braking).
  • C_TH — current is above CTH, or the current sensor is open.
  • P_Short — TRIGGER is low: the 0.5 s timer fired or the pressure sensor is out of range.
  • BSPD — the relay has dropped: the shutdown circuit is open.
